messages:
ivy: Heads-up — discovered confusing behavior when using REDWOOD_API_KEY with REDWOOD_PROJECT_ID set. Our runtime sometimes treats the key as org-scoped and rewrites the project header, causing the API to reject requests.

noah: which SDK/version?

ivy: python sdk 1.2.0 and node 0.10.0, repro in sample-service and in the CLI. Short repro: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_user_abc; export REDWOOD_PROJECT_ID=proj-ops; run service -> some requests 403 with message 'token not authorized for project'.

gina: sounds like an implicit re-scoping server-side. We should avoid implicit rewrites. Also devs are confused because local envs often have personal keys and they set project id from company docs.

auth-bot: Suggestion: add a clear validation endpoint /v1/auth/check which returns token owner and allowed projects.

noah: I propose SDK change: when both API_KEY and PROJECT_ID present, SDK should call auth/check once at startup and cache the result. If mismatch, emit error with actionable text and link to docs. Gate this behind REDWOOD_ENV_STRICT to avoid CI noise.

sam: runtime change: add 422 error code 'project_mismatch' with body suggesting check auth/check. That saves time.

ivy: also hit rotation issue — after we rotate a service key, agents that used cached mapping continue to call using old mapping for ~10s leading to spikes. Implement token-versioning broadcast in runtime to reduce mismatch windows.

gina: docs: add 'auth gotchas' page listing: ephemeral tokens, mixed personal/service keys, project env mismatches, and the REDWOOD_ENV_STRICT toggle.

noah: action items: 1) SDKs: startup validation + docs (noah) 2) API: add auth/check and clearer error code (sam) 3) sample-service: startup warning + troubleshooting blurb (gina) 4) runtime: token-broadcast during rotation (ivy). I'll create tickets and link them.

ivy: quick workaround we added in sample-service: if REDWOOD_API_KEY && REDWOOD_PROJECT_ID && REDWOOD_ENV_STRICT not set, print a conspicuous console warning and continue. If strict set, fail fast.

gina: can someone pick up the SDK tests for env permutations? if not, i'll take it next sprint.

noah: i'll do JS + python test matrix. tagging @sdk-team.

ivy: thanks everyone, this should cut down on the 'it worked locally' support threads. :pray:
